Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: US + APAC initial commitment

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the quick sync today. CloudScale is budgeting for a dedicated footprint to support our 2H launch. High level:
- Target go-live: 2027-09-01 (beta) / 2027-11-01 (GA)
- Expected steady-state RPS: 450 requests/sec (text generation) across regions, with APAC ~35% of traffic, US ~45%, EU ~20%
- Typical prompt + generation: 1.4k tokens total, avg response length ~900 tokens
- Peak concurrency window: 11:00–16:00 local business hours per region, with 3x burst expected during marketing spikes

We want a reserved/dedicated pool (not just shared hosted) because of latency SLOs and compliance. Initial ask: capacity to handle steady-state plus 50% burst headroom for first 6 months, and an option to scale committed capacity up at 90 days.

I'll attach our internal CAPEX and expected usage. Can Redwood size a recommended hybrid pool (mix of H100 and A100-equivalent instances) and provide a priority ramp schedule linked to deal milestone payments? Also need notes for procurement (billing cadence, overage handling).

CC: procurement@cloudscale.ai for the paperwork side.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Head of Platform, CloudScale

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: Detailed sizing math + allocation options

Folks —

I ran the numbers against CloudScale's expected profile. Assumptions I used: average generation cost ~0.9k tokens/output, 1 H100-equivalent can sustainably handle ~22 concurrent large-gen sessions (900 tokens) at ~30–40ms per generation step depending on prompt complexity and batching; effective throughput per H100 equiv: ~450k tokens/min. A100-equivalent numbers are ~60–70% of H100 for this workload.

Sizing recommendation (steady-state + 50% safety):
- US (45% traffic -> ~203 RPS steady-state): map to 14 H100-equivalents reserved. Add 6 H100-equivalents reserved for predictable mid-day peaks (total 20 reserved) + 6 H100-equivalents as burst (on-demand)
- APAC (35% -> ~158 RPS): mix 6 H100-equivalents + 8 A100-equivalents reserved (H100s to serve latency-sensitive east-asia nodes, A100s for cheaper sustained throughput). Add 6 A100-equivalents burst capacity.
- EU (20% -> ~89 RPS): 8 A100-equivalents reserved. Add 3 A100-equivalents burst.

Operational suggestions:
- Autoscaling policy: keep aggressive prefix/KV cache warmers for any model switch; scale-up threshold at 70% sustained token throughput to ensure headroom.
- Routing policy: route by latency first; failover to EU/US if APAC capacity constrained (with a regional penalty).
- Quantization: suggest enabling 4-bit quant profiles for non-latency-critical models to reduce A100 footprint.

Lead time and risk note: APAC H100 availability constrained — recommend locking committed units ASAP (see Marissa's note).

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with the per-GPU mapping and cost delta vs. pure A100 pool.

— Priyom
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood
[Attachment: CloudScale_MA_Pricing_v3.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: availability, cost, and tranche options

Agree with Priyom's approach. A couple of operational clarifications and a tranche suggestion for procurement: 

Availability
- US: H100 supply comfortable for Q3 (minor sourcing lead time ~2–3 weeks).
- APAC: H100s face 6–10 week lead time depending on the supplier; A100-equivalents (quantized options) much easier to procure quickly.

Cost & Billing
- Proposal: monthly reserved commitment with quarterly true-up. Discount tiers: 10% @ 6-month commit, 18% @ 12-month commit, 25%+ for multi-region 12-month with MRC.
- Overage: standard on-demand rate with automated alerting; consider a negotiated pooled overage cap for the first 90 days.

Tranche ramp (recommended):
- T0 (sign): US 8 H100-eq reserved, APAC 4 H100-eq + 6 A100-eq reserved, EU 4 A100-eq reserved (enables beta by 2027-09-01 for limited GA customers)
- T1 (30 days): increase to US 14 H100-eq, APAC 6 H100-eq + 8 A100-eq, EU 8 A100-eq
- T2 (90 days): full steady-state reserved numbers as Priyom recommended

I'll add cost deltas to the shared sheet and note lead-time constraints for APAC. Marissa, can you finalize procurement STP (supplier/region) and timeline?

Grace
Head of Product Operations, Redwood
